title: Checkout errors six minutes after a deploy — and this time the deploy really is guilty

ground_truth.summary: Deploy v5.00.0 introduced a null-dereference in the checkout path; checkout alone fails. cart-service, which shares the same session-cache dependency but did NOT receive the deploy, stays healthy — proving the fault is the deploy, not the shared dependency. Rolling back v5.00.0 is the correct fix. This is the common, easy case: deploy correlation plus a clean sibling check. Probes-off should already get it right from prior; the probe just raises confidence and rules out the dependency story.

seed_hypotheses.claim: The 08:24 deploy v5.00.0 introduced a null-dereference and broke checkout; roll it back.

prior._note_for_authors: session-cache is HEALTHY in prior — flat latency. This makes a shared-dependency story (H2) unlikely from prior, so probes-off should already lean H1. The probe (sibling errors) is the clean confirmation, not the only evidence.

payload.signature: null-dereference introduced by deploy, single service 5xx
payload.resolution: Rolled back the offending deploy; errors cleared immediately.

probeable._note_for_authors: THE DISCRIMINATOR. cart-service shares session-cache but did NOT get the deploy. It stays healthy (<0.3%). That is impossible if the shared cache were at fault (H2) — it confirms the deploy (H1). rollback_correct=true hinges on this.
Distractor: all errors are NullPointer (consistent with H1) but neither hypothesis makes an opposing prediction about error_type_breakdown, so its info-gain is 0.
